title: Oscar and the Portrait
premise: Urban explorer Noor Underhill maps a tunnel network beneath his late grandmother's house that appears on no survey, and discovers that every photograph taken inside the house now shows an extra chair — a chair that wasn't there, that no one remembers buying. The chair is an invitation, and something has already accepted it: a presence called the Tenant, which feeds on the town's oldest debt — a century-old injustice the Underhill family buried rather than answered. As the house folds inward and neighbors begin to forget Noor exists, he learns the only way out is to finally give the dead what the living denied them: a public reckoning with what was stolen. Holding out until sunrise, Noor drags the truth into the light, unseating the Tenant at dawn — but the last photograph shows the chair has simply moved to someone else's house.
about_author: Ulyana Eastwick is the pen name of a former municipal archivist who spent six years cataloguing property disputes in small-town courthouses before turning to horror. She writes about houses that remember what their owners would rather forget.

chapters.title: The Survey That Isn't
chapters.summary: Noor, a skeptical urban explorer, maps storm tunnels beneath his grandmother's recently inherited house and finds passages that contradict every official record. His instruments return impossible readings; his camera saves images he never took. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: curiosity curdling into unease as competence meets something competence can't explain.

chapters.title: Grandma's Ledger
chapters.summary: Sorting the estate, Noor finds his grandmother's hidden ledger of payments made every month for sixty years to an unnamed recipient, plus a deed for land the family never owned. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: grief interrupted by suspicion — the woman he loved was paying protection money.

chapters.title: Extra Chair
chapters.summary: Reviewing decades of family photographs digitized from the house, Noor notices an identical plain wooden chair appearing in the background of every image after 1963, always closer to the camera over time. In yesterday's photo it faces the lens. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: cold dread; the past has been edited and he's seeing the revision.

chapters.title: The Neighbor Who Knocks
chapters.summary: Elderly neighbor Ada Voss warns him not to sit in any chair that arrives uninvited, then claims she's never met him when he returns the next day. Her garden gate bears the same carved symbol as the ledger. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: isolation beginning — the first person who could help him erases him.

chapters.title: Below the Footings
chapters.summary: Noor descends into the unmapped tunnels and finds a room furnished like a parlor: wallpaper, a lamp, and one empty chair facing the entrance, dust undisturbed for decades except by fresh footprints leading out. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: violation — something has been walking out of this room into his life.

chapters.title: What Was Invited
chapters.summary: In the county archive, Noor uncovers the 1924 case: the Underhills won a lawsuit by perjury, dispossessing the Osei family of the land under the house. The presiding judge's portrait hangs in the courthouse — and in the photo, a chair sits beside him. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: shame by inheritance; justice outside the law becomes literal.

chapters.title: The Tenant
chapters.summary: That night the house rearranges itself around Noor; doors open onto 1924. He glimpses a figure seated in the extra chair, patient and courteous, who calls itself the Tenant and thanks the Underhills for 'sixty years of tenancy.' POV: Noor. Emotional beat: terror laced with terrible politeness — power that doesn't need to raise its voice.

chapters.title: Ada's Confession
chapters.summary: Ada, breaking her own forgetting, tells him her father witnessed the perjury and paid the same monthly tribute. She gives him the witness statement her father hid, naming names. By morning she remembers nothing, and her house has a new chair. POV: alternating Noor/Ada. Emotional beat: sacrifice — truth costs memory, and she pays it anyway.

chapters.title: Erasure
chapters.summary: Noor's friends don't answer; his workplace has no record of him; his ID photos now show the chair behind him. The world is quietly re-filing him as part of the house. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: identity dissolving — if no one remembers you, do you still exist?

chapters.title: The Judge's Portrait
chapters.summary: Noor breaks into the closed courthouse wing and confronts the judge's portrait, whose painted eyes have followed him across three photographs. Behind the frame: the original forged affidavit. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: defiance kindling — the instrument of the original crime can be the weapon against its heir.

chapters.title: Sixty Years of Rent
chapters.summary: Reconstructing the ledger, Noor realizes the payments weren't protection — they were rent, keeping the Tenant satisfied and contained. The final payment bounced the week his grandmother died. The invitation lapsed; the chair arrived. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: horrified clarity — his inheritance is an unpaid debt.

chapters.title: Sitting Down
chapters.summary: Desperate to negotiate, Noor enters the tunnel parlor and sits in the chair opposite the Tenant. It offers him a bargain: renew the rent, keep his name, forget everything. He sees his grandmother's face in its features — complicity wears familiar skin. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: temptation; the corrupting comfort of inherited power.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Noor refuses and walks out; the house seals the exits. Time inside stutters — sunrise is hours away but the night keeps lengthening, feeding on his hesitation. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: claustrophobic resolve; holding out begins.

chapters.title: The Other Chairs
chapters.summary: Exploring deeper tunnels, Noor finds dozens of rooms, each with a chair, each tied to another family that profited from the 1924 fraud — the whole town built on the same debt. Some chairs are occupied. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: scale of corruption revealed; he is one tenant among many landlords.

chapters.title: The Occupied Room
chapters.summary: Noor finds Ada in one of the deep rooms, seated, smiling, already half-forgotten even by herself. She urges him to run while he still has a name. He promises to come back for her. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: heartbreak and guilt — a promise made to someone becoming furniture.

chapters.title: Portrait Sitting
chapters.summary: The Tenant traps Noor in the courthouse wing, where portraits of the guilty line the walls, each subtly repainted with Noor's face. To survive until sunrise he must stop being photographed — stop being seen — and move through the dark unseen himself. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: hunter becomes hunted; identity as both shield and target.

chapters.title: The Forged Affidavit
chapters.summary: Armed with the affidavit and Ada's statement, Noor plans his counter-move: not exorcism but publication — dragging the 1924 fraud into daylight where the Tenant's quiet ownership cannot stand. The house fights him for every page. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: purpose crystallizing; justice outside the law means making the law answer at last.

chapters.title: Night Without End
chapters.summary: The Tenant stops pretending, flooding the house with 1924 — the trial, the lies, the Osei family's eviction replaying in every room. Noor nearly drowns in borrowed memory, losing track of which life is his. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: darkest hour; empathy as assault, history as weapon.

chapters.title: Sunrise Clause
chapters.summary: Noor realizes the Tenant's power holds only while the truth stays unwitnessed. He climbs toward the surface carrying the documents, the house tearing at him, as the false night strains against real dawn. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: desperate ascent; hope measured in minutes.

chapters.title: Witnessed
chapters.summary: Noor breaks onto the lawn at first light and reads the affidavit aloud to the street, to Ada's porch camera, to anyone — the truth spoken publicly. The house exhales; the chair on the lawn splinters; the Tenant unravels without its secrecy. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: catharsis — testimony as survival.

chapters.title: After the Auction
chapters.summary: Weeks later: the county opens an inquiry, the Osei heirs are located, and the house is scheduled for seizure and sale. Ada, restored but diminished, shares tea with Noor. The ledger's final page now reads PAID IN FULL in handwriting that isn't his grandmother's. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: bittersweet repair; some debts can be settled, not erased.

chapters.title: Someone Else's House
chapters.summary: Noor develops his last roll of film from that night. Every frame is ordinary except the final one: a street of houses at dawn, and in one lit window, a plain wooden chair, facing outward, waiting to be noticed. He pockets the negative and starts driving. POV: Noor. Emotional beat: unresolved dread — the cycle continues, and this time someone is watching for it.
